post.summary: Send one message to the investigation assistant
post.description: With no AI provider, with every AI feature off or with the assistant off this path answers 403 with the reason ai-off. A client that sends `Accept: application/x-ndjson` gets the turn as a stream of lines (application/x-ndjson): `step` events that say which step is about to run (`routing`, `reading-view`, `reading` with the tool, its label and subject, `answering`), then one `answer` line that is exactly the JSON answer, or an `error` line for a failure that has no turn answer after the first line; a request refused before the handler runs is answered with its HTTP status as for any client, and a stream is never idempotent. No line holds anything a model wrote before the answer. Takes a message as typed and the keys of the elements in view, checks that the investigation is the caller's and belongs to the source, and answers in exactly one route (view, ask or refuse). A refusal carries a fixed sentence chosen by the server; no word of the model is returned.

200.description: The turn: a refusal with its cause and fixed sentence; the not-answered turn of the view route; the answer of the ask route (Ask's answer, with a step and a coverage line for a result that was read); unavailable, too-large, too-long or continue-invalid, each with nothing sent or read as it says

get.summary: The caller's own thread of an investigation, as the kind and end of each turn
get.description: With no AI provider, with every AI feature off or with the assistant off this path answers 403 with the reason ai-off. Answers the caller's own thread of one of their investigations: for each turn its order, time, route, outcome, cause, intent, the number of things it cited and the number of reads. It holds no text of a question or an answer and no reference, hash, token or run id; a thread holds references and metadata only, is cleared when the investigation is closed, archived or deleted, and is never used for training. The answer holds the most recent turns of the thread (100 by default, a setting) and earlierTurns, how many older ones there are (nothing stored is trimmed; the bound only limits what one answer and the panel hold). previousThreadClearedAt says when the caller's previous thread was cleared, when they have no thread since; it is null otherwise.

200.description: The caller's turns in order, and when their previous thread was cleared

post.summary: Draft a cited summary of the view on screen
post.description: Present only when the deployment has switched the AI preview on; otherwise this path answers 404. Takes the references of the elements in view, never their content, checks that the investigation is the caller's and for the source, reads the elements again through the gate for the signed-in person, and drafts a short neutral summary in which every sentence cites the elements it rests on. Administrators and investigators only. Requires an Idempotency-Key: a repeat with the same key, person and request answers the first answer again with the header Idempotent-Replay: true, after the person's access has been checked again; a provider failure or a time limit is not kept, so a retry runs again. The request takes no query string. The draft is not stored or exported unless the person copies it to notes or includes it in an export.

200.description: The draft (status ok, with the sentences, the text sent, the model, the calls made and a sealed summaryToken), a view over the element cap or the size guard (tooLarge), the time limit reached (timeLimit), or a failure to draft with a fixed kind (failed). With the header Idempotent-Replay: true when it is the first answer again

post.description: Present only when an AI provider is configured (or the deployment has switched the AI preview on); otherwise this path answers 404 (not mounted), or 403 (ACCESS_DENIED with the reason ai-off) when the feature is switched off. The token must be the caller's, for this investigation, within 30 minutes, from the policy version and the word list version in force; any other is ACCESS_DENIED, as is an investigation the caller may not write. A stale version is CONFLICTED_VIEW_VERSION; a full list or an entry over its bounds is INVALID_REQUEST with the reason ai-notes-full or ai-notes-entry-too-large. The audit event holds the run and counts, never a sentence.

get.summary: Load one entity of a source, without its neighbors
get.description: Reads the node of one entity type with one stable ID through the gate, as the calling principal. The reference travels as three percent-encoded path segments. A browser removes a segment of dots, however it is written, so an entity type or a stable ID made only of dots and tildes is sent with a tilde in front, and the server takes one tilde off such a segment; every other value is sent as it is. A segment that is a lone tilde stands for no value and is refused with INVALID_REQUEST. The node, the audit record and the stored investigation all hold the real value, never the form on the wire. The stable ID is matched as text and, when the text is a canonical 64-bit integer, as that integer too, so a source whose IDs are integers is found. mask=true masks the personal-data fields of the node and any title built from them. The node carries the quality flag duplicate-stable-id when the source holds more than one node with the ID; the node shown is then the first by element ID. The answer says nothing about whether the entity exists in another source.

A token of another source or entity type, a malformed token and a masked raw value of a keyed type are INVALID_REQUEST, one answer for all. No value or token is logged.

get.summary: The caller's investigations, a page at a time, across every source the caller may read
get.description: Reads Postgres only; no source is read. Lists the caller's own undeleted investigations of one status (open when status is left out), the most recently edited first and, between equal times, the larger id first. Investigations of a configured source the policy does not let the caller read are left out without a record; investigations of a source no longer in the configuration are listed with sourceState removed. limit is a whole number from 1 to 100 (25 when left out); a larger one is QUERY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED with the maximum in details.maxPage, and 0 is INVALID_REQUEST. nextCursor is a signed, expiring string that is null on the last page; it is valid for the same caller, status, source and q, and anything else is CURSOR_INVALIDATED. A row edited or added between two calls is never repeated, and may be missing from the later pages. status, source (a source id) and q (2 to 200 characters, a fragment of the title or of the case reference, matched without regard to case) narrow the list; an unknown source or one the caller may not read gives an empty list. sort is lastEdited, the only order; any other query parameter is refused. sourceAlias is the alias the product stored for the source. save is saved, with the time of the named view, when the caller's draft equals the named view it was last saved as, and unsaved otherwise. nodeCount and edgeCount are the loaded-item counts of the caller's draft at its last save, null when they were made under another policy version. matching is the exact number of investigations the filters select. counts describes the library whatever the filters: the open investigations that could be listed, the sources they are on and the named views of the caller's investigations of any status with the newest time any of them was updated (null when there is none), all exact; the rows, matching and counts are read at one snapshot.

The title is the display name of the entity type and the stable ID, never built from a personal-data property, and is cut at 200 characters with a final ellipsis when longer. With a caseRef, the caller's own open, undeleted investigation with the same source, case reference and starting entity is returned instead (200, created false); without one, every call creates an investigation. An investigation whose source now points at another database is returned without reading the source: sourceState is repointed and there is no entity. mask asks for the personal-data fields of the returned entity to be masked.

put.description: Writes Postgres only; no source is read. The body is { title, expectedVersion }: the title is stored as typed (not empty or only whitespace, at most 200 code points, no NUL and no unpaired surrogate) and expectedVersion is the investigation's version, which the answer's ETag carries. The version goes up by one and last_edited_at does not change; the title the investigation already has changes nothing and answers the same version. A closed or archived investigation is refused with CONFLICT and details.reason investigation-read-only (this check comes before the version check); a stale expectedVersion is CONFLICT without a reason. The investigation leaves every ordinary list and every route except restore and the deleted list: deleted_at is the database time, purge_after is that time plus the configured number of days (retention.deleted_investigations_days, 30 by default) and the version goes up by one. The status, the draft, the named views and the last-edited time are not touched. It works whatever the status. An investigation that is already deleted, another user's or unknown is NOT_FOUND.

post.summary: Close, archive or reopen an investigation of the caller
post.description: Writes Postgres only; no source is read. The body is { status, expectedVersion } with status open, closed or archived. Allowed changes: open to closed, open to archived, closed to open, closed to archived and archived to open; archived to closed is CONFLICT with details.reason status-change-not-allowed. Closing sets closedAt; archiving sets archivedAt and keeps an earlier closedAt; reopening clears both. The version goes up by one and last_edited_at does not change. A request for the status the investigation already has answers 200 with the same version and writes nothing, whatever expectedVersion it carries. A stale expectedVersion is CONFLICT without a reason. Closing, archiving and reopening are audited as investigation.close, investigation.archive and investigation.reopen, with a success event recorded after the change is committed (a failed write records a failed event instead); if the sink rejects the success event the change stays and the answer is INTERNAL_ERROR. An identifier that does not exist, is not a UUID, belongs to another user or is deleted gives the same 404.

post.summary: Export what the person is showing as JSON, CSV or a picture
post.description: Reads the referenced entities and relationships through the gate (never the browser's copy). For json and csv it builds one file and keeps it on the server's disk until it expires. For png it builds and keeps nothing: it audits the export and answers the header and the file name, and the browser draws the picture (the picture is drawn from the view as the browser holds it, or from data it read with the same flag); a view in which something was left out because the person may not read or export it, or it no longer resolves, is refused with details.reason export-view-changed, so the picture never shows more than a file would. JSON is one file; CSV is one zip holding entities.csv and relationships.csv. mask: true (any format; absent means false) masks the fields marked pii in the file while the server builds it, so the stored file is the masked one, and the header and the audit state how many fields are masked; a policy can mask more, never less. The same Idempotency-Key with another mask, or with the flag present in one and absent in the other, is CONFLICT. Every file begins with a header that states the source, the time, that the file is a partial view, how many items are shown and how many are not yet retrieved (with the count quality), and the masking state. Items the person may not export are left out without a count. `Idempotency-Key` is required (16 to 64 letters, digits, _ and -); a retry with the same key returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replay: true`. A closed or archived investigation can be exported.

post.summary: Search a source for the entities whose search properties equal a text
post.description: Matches the whole text, as stored and case-sensitive, against every configured, indexed search property of the source in one read through the gate, and as the integer too when the text is a canonical 64-bit integer. The answer holds at most cap entities in exact (25, or the source's max_page when lower); counts.exact is exact when the group has no next page and a lowerBound of the hits held (cap, or fewer when normalization left rows out of a capped read) when the read found more, and exactNextCursor is then the cursor of the next page of the group (POST /v1/search/entities/more); each of related and evidence holds its own nextCursor the same way; searchable is false when no property was left to search. The text is 1 to 200 characters. entityTypes and matchModes (a non-empty list of different names each, absent when the search is not narrowed, refused with typeahead true) narrow the search to those entity types of the mapping of the source (the exact and the related group; the evidence group is not narrowed by entity type) and to the groups of those match modes (exact, related, evidence; a group that is not chosen is not read and is not searchable in the answer); a name the mapping does not know is INVALID_REQUEST. mask asks for the personal-data fields of the entities to be masked, and a personal-data property is then not searched. dropped and warnings are the normalize stage's: rows left out, by reason, and one sentence for each. disabledTypes names each search property that was not searched, with its entity type and why (index-unavailable: no online index; index-building: its index is populating; index-failed: its index failed), and typeSearched false when none of the properties of the type was searched; the other properties of the type are searched. related is the second group: the records whose reference properties (named by the mapping) hold the text, from one read of their own with its own limit, capped and counted like exact (counts in related.count, scope search:related); the related read adds nothing to exact or to its count: an entity is in exact only through its own exact match, and one that is both appears in both groups. related.searchable is false when no reference property was left to read (none configured, only personal-data ones while masked, or every type left out) and related.disabledTypes names each reference property left out the same way. evidence is the third group: the relationships whose evidence properties (named by the mapping) hold the text, from one read of their own with its own limit, capped and counted like exact (counts in evidence.count, scope search:evidence, in supporting relationships: a stored hit is one, an aggregate hit its members). A hit on a relationship row that has a stable_id is { supports, records, rules }: supports is the stored reference { sourceId, type, from, to, stableId } of the relationship. A hit on a row with no stable_id is { aggregate, members, memberCount, rules }: aggregate is { type, from, to } with the references of both ends, members are its relationships on this page, each { records, observedAt? } (a member has no ID: the element ID of the source never leaves the server, and the next page continues from a position the signed cursor holds), and memberCount is the members listed, a lowerBound when another page may hold more. records are the values of all the evidence properties of a relationship, each { sourceRecordId } or, for a value that is neither text nor a number, { property, unreadable: true }; rules are the configured rules of the mapping that use its relationship type. evidence.searchable is false when no relationship row was left to read, and evidence.disabledRelationshipTypes names each evidence property not searched with its row and the same reasons. With typeahead true the text is 2 to 200 characters and the answer also holds startsWith: the entities whose search property starts with the text, apart from the entities in exact, with its own count (exact up to and including cap, a lowerBound above it, never counted as exact matches), dropped and warnings; it is one more read, capped at cap and not paged (it has no nextCursor, so a common prefix never makes the source read every match), and shares the one schema read. A type-ahead request reads neither the related nor the evidence group: their searchable is false in its answer. A group whose read failed with a code of its own (QUERY_TIMEOUT with timeoutMs, SOURCE_BUSY, RATE_LIMITED or INTERNAL_ERROR) while another group answered is empty, has a count of quality unknown with no value, and is named in failures (always present, empty when every read answered); a retry repeats the whole search. When every group that was read fails, or an error means the same for every group, the search fails as a whole with the status and error of the read. facets (every answer that is not a type-ahead answer; a type-ahead answer holds neither facets nor filters) is the size of the whole match set, whatever is selected, from one read of its own: searchable is false when no target was left to count; otherwise entityType holds an entry for each entity type that has an eligible search or reference target (the entities of that type matched by either, each counted once), matchMode an entry for each match mode with an eligible target (exact, related, evidence; evidence in supporting relationships) and total the entities matched by any target; every count is exact up to and including the source's count cap (heavy_op_threshold, 500 by default) and a lowerBound of the cap above it, and an exact count is never lower than the hits its group holds (scopes search:facet:entityType, search:facet:matchMode, search:facet:total), and none is the sum of others. A facet counts the matches in the source, a group shows what the normalize stage can name, so a facet can be higher than its group by the records normalization dropped. The facet read is one more read and is not a result group: when it fails with a code of its own it is named in failures with the group facets, facets is then searchable with an unknown total and no entry, and every group is kept; it is never counted among the groups that failed. filters is the selection the answer was made for (entity types and match modes, each empty when the request did not narrow). The text is never logged and never part of an error.

Only the creator may do any of this: a shared pattern of another person is `ACCESS_DENIED`, and a private or deleted one of another person is `NOT_FOUND`. Sharing a pattern whose conditions hold what the mapping now marks as personal data is refused. A stale version is `CONFLICT`, and a body that changes nothing, names a field of the other kind, or holds a definition, parameters or entity that save would refuse is `INVALID_REQUEST`. A name equal to the stored one with the current version is a change like any other. Another person's pattern, a deleted one and an identifier that is not a pattern's answer `NOT_FOUND`. post.description: Answers, for a pattern definition that is acceptable for the source, what it will read: the display names of the types it starts from and arrives at, the relationship types and the direction of each step, each condition with its operator and typed values, each window (the relationship types that carry no date are named apart, as the window does not filter them), and the limits of the source a run holds to (`max_hops`, `max_page` and the count the source stops at), each as a number and as words the client joins. While masking is asked, a condition on personal data answers `personal-data-masked` and no preview, so no such value is shown. A definition that is not acceptable answers the problems of `POST /v1/patterns/validate`, and no preview. post.summary: Run a pattern definition from one starting entity, in one bounded read
post.description: Validates the definition against the source (as the validation route does), then runs it through the gate from the entity in `anchor`, whose type is the definition's anchor type: one bounded read that follows each step over the listed relationship types, each step cut at the source's count cap, an entity with more relationships than the cap or on a stop-list not traversed. Answers the matches (the entity the last step reaches, with one path to it: the entities between and the relationship of each hop), the nodes and relationships that are shown, the notices and the count with its quality: exact only when nothing cut or skipped the read, a lower bound otherwise. A definition with a problem is refused (the validation route says which); more steps than the source's `max_hops` is refused with `details.maxHops`. An estimate is read first, in the same request, through the gate: a count of the entities the last step reaches, read with the run's own bounds and stopped at the source's count cap plus one. When it read more than the threshold the run does not start and the answer is `status: "heavy"` with `estimate` (a `lowerBound` whose value is the threshold, scope `template:pattern:estimate`), `threshold`, `continueLimit` and no rows; an estimate that fails, is cancelled or runs out of time ends the request with that error. `continue` continues a run that stopped as heavy: it skips the estimate and returns a first page of at most 25. get.description: Lists the built-in templates a pattern can bind, in a fixed order, each enabled for the source: its id, version, a generic name, the description that tells the template from the others, and `paramsSchema`, a JSON Schema generated from the contract schema of the parameters a caller sends. The schema states the shape: every input the run route accepts passes it, and the route also refuses inputs it accepts (a date that is not on the calendar, a range in the wrong order or too wide, a stable ID longer than the bound counted in UTF-16 units, the members a preset fixes, a name the mapping does not have, a limit or a hop count above the source budget). Lists the presets of the source as its profile gives them, in mapping order, and nothing else; a source with no presets lists none. Reads no source and no database. An unknown source is NOT_FOUND; a missing, empty or repeated sourceId, or another query member, is INVALID_REQUEST.

post.summary: Run a built-in template or one preset of a source, from one starting entity, in one bounded read
post.description: Runs the template named by the path, or the preset of the source that the path names, through the gate. `params` is checked by the template's own schema; for the shared-attribute template it holds `ref` (the entity type and stable ID of the starting entity), `attributeType` and `via` (given by a preset, and refused when a preset also receives them), an optional `window` (`{days}` or `{from, to}`), `minShared` and `limit`. The answer holds the other entities that share an attribute node with the starting entity (`matchIds`, never the starting entity), the starting entity, the shared attribute nodes and the evidence relationships, in the nodes and in the relationships of the answer, a `count` of the matches that is exact when the run was not cut and a lowerBound when it was cut or a bound of the read was hit, and `notices` (stopListSkipped, noStopList, undatedExcluded, readBounded, evidenceCut). For the linked-entities template `params` holds `ref`, `targetType` and `via` (a list of relationship types; given by a preset, which names one, and refused when a preset also receives them), an optional `direction` (out, in or both; omitted, the stored direction read from the starting entity), `maxHops` (1 by default; a number above the lower of 2 and the source's `max_hops` is QUERY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED with the cap in `details.maxHops`), `window` and `limit`; the answer holds the entities of the target type reached in one or two hops (`matchIds`, never the starting entity), `links` (how each match was reached: its hop count and, at two hops, the entity in between), the nodes and the relationships, a `count` exact when the run was not cut and a lowerBound when it was cut, a bound was hit or a supernode or a stop-listed entity was not traversed, and `notices` that also include windowNotApplied (the relationship types a window could not apply to) and supernodesSkipped (the entities that were not traversed). `Idempotency-Key` is required (16 to 64 letters, digits, _ and -); a retry with the same key returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replay: true`. An id that is neither a preset of the source nor a built-in template, an entity type the source does not map, or a source that is not configured or that the person may not read is NOT_FOUND. `mask` is part of the request because the nodes follow it.

A draft holds references and never property values, so a reopened investigation gets its items back here. The call counts as one request; every item is read by the template the matching single read uses, so the masking, the count labels and the limits are those of the single reads. An item that no longer resolves is listed under missing, once, whatever the cause (gone from the source, a type or rule no longer mapped, or not readable by the person); nothing says which. The relationships come without their ends: the entities are asked for in the same or an earlier call. A derived relationship is returned only when its rule still finds it and every one of its ends and supports is readable. A reference of another source is SOURCE_MISMATCH; a reference of a keyed entity type that is not a token of this deployment for this source and type is INVALID_REQUEST. post.summary: One page of the neighbors of a node for each asked neighbor type
post.description: Reads one page of at most `limit` relationships (the source default page when absent; above the source maximum the answer is QUERY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED) for each asked neighbor type, newest first by the observed time of the mapping row and undated last, with the neighbor nodes. The types are read one after another under one read lease and the answer holds a page and a cursor for each; a failure in any of them answers the failure and no page. A cursor continues one type and is refused with CURSOR_INVALIDATED when altered, expired or minted for another source, person, policy version, sort, neighbor type, relationship types, direction or node. Relationships of a type with no stable ID are returned as aggregate relationships with their member count. A `window` (`{days}` or `{from, to}`; absent, all time) keeps only the relationships whose own observed time is in it: each relationship type is windowed by its own `observed_at`, a relationship with no usable time is not in it and a type with no `observed_at` is not filtered. `{days: n}` is read as whole UTC days (from 00:00 UTC of the day n days before today up to 00:00 UTC of tomorrow), so a cursor lives until the UTC day changes. The answer then holds `window` (the two instants) and, for each page, `window` (`applied` full, partial or none, `notAppliedTo`, and `undatedLeftOut` when counted); counts from a windowed read have the scope `expand:window` and are not the degree of the entity.
